title: Revenue Management Guideline: Existing-Customer Rent Increases on the Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement
content:
**1. Increases.** The company may raise the rent of an existing tenant of a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement with an existing-customer rate increase notice. An increase notice may be sent only when the handling date is not earlier than the move-in date plus the class's first-increase wait in months, and not earlier than the last rent change date plus the class's interval in months. Months are calendar months, counted to the same day of the later month or that month's last day when the day does not exist. Rate increase notices are issued only to rentals in active status.

**2. Size (former wording).** This clause is no longer in force: "The new rent is at most the current monthly rent times one plus the class's largest single increase, rounded down to the cent." It has been superseded by the current increase-limit basis.

**3. Effective date and notice.** The effective date is the first rent due date that falls at least the class's notice period in calendar days after the notice date. The new rent is applied to the agreement only when the handling date is not earlier than the notice date plus the class's notice period. Notice and request windows count calendar days starting the day after the notice date, and the last counted day is included.

**4. Retention concessions.** The former clause "A tenant who calls about a noticed increase may be given one retention concession that gives back the class's retention share of the increase, rounded down to the cent, with the same effective date and pointing at the increase" is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current retention concession basis. A retention concession may be granted only when the handling date is not later than the increase notice date plus the class's request window in days. Retention concessions on the agreement — those whose notice date falls in the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date, inclusive — must number fewer than the class's retention concessions per rolling 12 months. An increase that has already taken effect is not reduced by a concession; a rental with a move-out notice gets no concession. When a concession is granted, the agreement rent applied on the effective date is the concession's new rent.

**5. Prepaid rate lock.** While a Bluegate Prepaid Rent Plan in active status covers the rental, no increase notice is sent and no increase takes effect before the prepaid term ends.

## Timing worked through (hypothetical class: 6-month first wait, 11-month interval, 30-day notice, 30-day request window)

| Item | Dates | Result |
|---|---|---|
| First-increase wait | move-in 31 August 2026, plus 6 months | 28 February 2027 |
| Interval | last rent change 15 March 2026, plus 11 months | 15 February 2027 |
| Earliest notice | both dates reached | 28 February 2027 |
| Effective date | notice 1 March 2027, billing day the 10th; day 30 after notice is 31 March | 10 April 2027 |
| Request window | notice 1 March 2027 | through 31 March 2027, inclusive |

A concession asked for on 31 March in this example is inside the window; on 1 April it is outside.

superseded_clauses: The new rent is at most the current monthly rent times one plus rate_increase_max_pct, rounded down to the cent.

A tenant who calls about a noticed increase may be given one retention_concession that gives back retention_concession_pct_of_increase of the increase, rounded down to the cent, with the same effective date and its source_rate_change_id pointing at the increase.
